why: Subsets by include or exclude: every element is in or out, so a depth-first walk that decides element 0, then 1, and so on reaches all 2^n subsets at its leaves; the required order (by size, then by index positions) is a sort afterwards, or the same backtracking run once per size k.
hints: How many choices does each element have, and so how many subsets are there in total?
dfs(i, path): if i == n record a copy of path; otherwise recurse once without nums[i] and once with it (append, recurse, pop).
Sort the recorded index lists by (length, indices), or for k in 0..n backtrack choosing the next index greater than the last until k are chosen. O(n * 2^n).
pitfalls: Keep elements in input order inside a subset ([3,-1], not [-1,3]); do not sort nums.
The usual include/exclude DFS produces a different order; group by size as required.
